narrative:
The model estimates a 20% chance that you will fail your final year, which is why the school requires you to take remedial courses as a precaution. Although this probability is not extremely high, the system flags it as enough of a risk to warrant extra support.

Three factors stood out most in the prediction. First, your very high alcohol consumption during the week was the strongest influence, pushing the outcome toward failure. Most students who passed reported very low weekday drinking, so your level stands out as unusual and appears to have hurt your predicted performance. Second, having no past class failures worked in your favor and pulled the prediction back toward passing. Third, choosing this school for its reputation also nudged the result slightly toward passing, since that reason is more common among students who ultimately succeed.

Even though your strong study habits, desire for higher education, and lack of previous failures are positive signals, the model weighed your weekday drinking habits more heavily. To improve, consider cutting back on alcohol during the school week, as this seems to be the main factor working against you. Taking the remedial courses seriously and replacing some of that time with focused study or rest could help turn the 20% risk into a much stronger chance of passing.
